decisions.reason: A reference-class electrometer is core dosimetry know-how where the firm's deep absorptive capacity and accredited calibration lab let it interpret feedback and refine the flagship product.
Risk management software builds on the firm's QA software integration capabilities and supports its patient-safety direction, though software outside measurement carries somewhat more uncertainty.
A CT image quality phantom extends established imaging QA knowledge, so the firm can readily assimilate customer results and improve it.
Mammography is farther from the firm's core knowledge, but it belongs to the imaging QA line the firm is expanding, so it is likely kept while the firm builds related expertise.
Distant from the core and overlapping with the other mammography phantom, which raises consolidation risk, but the firm will likely keep it as part of its imaging portfolio in the near term.
A flagship imaging QA instrument line building on established measurement expertise fits the strategic direction and is very unlikely to be dropped.
